title: Facilities Coordinator - 12 Month FTC - Hull
description:
Facilities Coordinator - 12 Month Fixed-Term Contract Location: Hull, East Yorkshire
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Job Type: Full Time 12 Month FTC
Hours: 35 hours per week
Working Pattern: Hybrid / Agile Working
Travel: Regular travel to UK offices, with occasional overnight stays

An excellent opportunity has arisen for a proactive and organised Facilities Coordinator to join the Facilities team of a well-established and forward-thinking legal services organisation based in Hull.

This is a varied and hands-on position, supporting the day-to-day management, maintenance and smooth running of multiple office locations across the UK.

Working closely with colleagues, landlords, contractors and external suppliers, you will help ensure that offices remain safe, compliant, well-maintained and efficient, while supporting facilities projects, office moves and workplace improvements.

Offering hybrid working, an excellent benefits package and exposure to multi-site facilities management, this opportunity would suit someone who enjoys a varied role combining practical problem-solving, facilities administration and health and safety responsibilities.

The Role As Facilities Coordinator, your responsibilities will include:
- Coordinating day-to-day facilities operations, building maintenance and repairs across multiple UK offices.
- Liaising with landlords, maintenance contractors, suppliers and third-party service providers.
- Supporting workplace health and safety compliance, including risk assessments and workstation assessments.
- Monitoring outstanding actions and ensuring facilities and safety issues are addressed promptly.
- Assisting with office moves, refurbishments, minor maintenance works and facilities improvement projects.
- Maintaining accurate facilities records, compliance documentation and building safety information.
- Supporting the review and development of facilities policies, procedures and processes.
- Managing facilities-related requests and tickets through Salesforce.
- Coordinating and booking complex business travel arrangements.
- Supporting internal and external events and ensuring offices operate effectively.

About You We are looking for a practical, organised and approachable individual who enjoys taking ownership of tasks and ensuring things run smoothly.

Essential requirements:
- Previous experience or a good working knowledge of office health and safety procedures.
- IOSH qualification or currently working towards one.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Confident communication skills and the ability to build relationships with colleagues, contractors and suppliers.
- Good IT skills, particularly Microsoft Excel, Word and PowerPoint.
- A proactive, flexible and hands-on approach to problem-solving.
- Ability to work independently and make sound decisions.
- Full UK driving licence and access to a car.
- Willingness to travel regularly between UK offices, including occasional overnight stays.

Desirable experience:
- Previous experience in Facilities Coordination, Facilities Management or Office Management.
- Knowledge of Health and Safety Executive (HSE) guidance.
- First Aid at Work qualification.
- Fire Marshal training or certification.
- Experience supporting multi-site office operations.

Previous experience within a law firm or legal services organisation is not essential.

What's on Offer?
- Competitive salary, dependent on experience.
- 12-month fixed-term contract.
- Hybrid and agile working arrangements.
- 35-hour working week.
- Private pension.
- Medical insurance.
- Generous annual leave allowance.
- Supportive and collaborative working environment.
- Opportunity to gain experience supporting facilities operations across multiple UK locations.

Interested? If you're an experienced Facilities Coordinator, Facilities Assistant, Office Coordinator or Office Manager with a strong understanding of workplace health and safety, I'd be keen to hear from you.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a progressive organisation offering flexibility, variety and a supportive working environment.

title: Finance & Reporting Administrator
description:
Finance & Reporting Administrator
Location: Hessle
Salary: £28,000 - £32,000 Pro rata

We're incredibly proud to be working with this independent, family-run business where people genuinely matter and are what make it such a great place to work.

Our client is a well-established UK services company providing a personal, often bespoke service to commercial customers nationwide. Offering 20 hours per week with flexible working hours, this is a fantastic opportunity to enjoy a varied finance role while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.

You'll join a friendly, close-knit team where your contribution and ideas will be valued. The business is keen to embrace new technology and smarter ways of working, so there's plenty of opportunity to use your initiative and make a real difference.

The Opportunity:
As a Finance & Reporting Administrator, you'll play a key role in:
- Managing supplier commissions, invoicing, payments and resolving discrepancies.
- Maintaining accurate financial records using Sage, including processing debits, credits and bank reconciliations.
- Updating client databases, ensuring pricing changes and information are recorded accurately.
- Preparing weekly and monthly reports covering sales performance, financial results, budgets and key business information.
- Supporting the team with financial queries and identifying opportunities to improve processes, including the use of AI technology.

About You:
We're looking for someone who can bring:
- Previous experience in finance administration, accounts support or a similar role.
- Strong numerical skills and excellent attention to detail.
- Good Excel skills and confidence using financial systems, ideally Sage.
- Excellent organisation, initiative and a proactive approach to problem-solving.
- A friendly, positive personality and the ability to work well within a small team.

You'll also be comfortable with technology and open to learning new ways of working. Previous AI experience isn't needed, just curiosity and a willingness to embrace new ideas.

The Benefits and Package:
- Salary: £28,000 to £32,000 pro rata.
- 20 hours per week with flexible working hours.
- A welcoming, supportive and close-knit team.
- A varied role with responsibility and the freedom to use your initiative.
- The opportunity to contribute ideas, improve processes and develop your skills.

How to Apply:
This Finance & Reporting Administrator opportunity is being managed by Consortium Professional Recruitment, a trusted recruitment partner.

If you're looking for a rewarding part-time finance role where your experience and ideas will be valued, we'd love to hear from you. Please apply with your CV attached.

Consortium Professional Recruitment Ltd are a professional level recruitment consultancy specialising in the delivery of high relevance recruitment services on behalf of our clients across the UK. We regularly receive large responses to our advertising which can make providing individual feedback to every applicant challenging. If you haven't received a reply from us within 14 days of your application, we regret to say your application has been unsuccessful on this occasion. title: Accounts Receivable Administrator
description:
Role: Accounts Receivable Administrator

Location: Hessle, HU13

Are you a proactive and driven Accounts Receivable Administrator with great communication skills? Can you manage and support company credit control by taking responsibility for your own book of debtor accounts?

Then Scientific Laboratory Supplies (SLS) is the right fit for you. Join us and contribute to our mission of being the UK's largest independent supplier of laboratory equipment, chemicals, and consumables.

We have an exciting opportunity available for a Credit Controller to join our finance team based in Hessle, HU13, on a full-time, permanent basis.

Job Summary:

The Accounts Receivable Administrator will join the SLS Finance team and contribute to all areas within the finance function. The successful candidate will be asked to support the busy credit control function in the office but must be willing to provide support as needed to other areas of the finance function which will include communicating with colleagues, external parties, customers, and vendors.

Key Responsibilities:
- Take a proactive role in managing and supporting company credit control by taking responsibility for own book of debtor accounts.
- Use all forms of communication (email, letters, and telephone) to professionally contact debtors and ensure payment of outstanding invoices.
- Support the ongoing process of credit checking new customers and open new credit accounts ensuring the company has all the relevant information.
- Support and resolve all problems experienced in the credit control function including providing copy invoices, obtaining proof of delivery.
- Work closely with colleagues in Sales and Customer Services to resolve any customer queries and enquiries to progress matters to a satisfactory conclusion.
- Report regularly to the Accounts Office Manager on outstanding issues and promptly inform them of potential debtors' problems.
- When required, help colleagues to manage the "slsledger" email inbox, resolving enquiries quickly and effectively and to pass enquiries onto colleagues in both Finance and other departments for resolution.
- Maintain financial system records and enter data accurately.

Perform general clerical duties when required, including, but not limited to, typing, mailing, filing correspondence and answering telephone calls.

Ideal Candidate:
- Prior experience of working in a credit control / accounts receivable function.
- Comfortable with IT.
- Strong literacy and numeracy skills.
- Interpersonal skills, appreciation of good internal and external customer service behaviour.
- Be organised, methodical, self-motivated, and driven.
- Responsive and re-active.
- Good customer-facing and personal relationship skills.
- Be able to communicate at all levels.
- Ability to work within a flexible team.

About us:

SLS are the UK's largest independent supplier of laboratory equipment, chemicals, and consumables. Because of our independence, we have a unique approach to sourcing and supplying the highest quality, best value products, and brands. Supplying to a wide range of sectors, provides a diverse and interesting customer base as well as providing countless opportunity to grow and expand.

With customers all over the UK, we are a stable and growing company who have an excellent reputation in the market.

We are passionate about our people and have developed a strong team dynamic who are welcoming and supportive of new individuals, joining the company with a brilliant management team to support you as you find your feet in the role.

We are also proud to be a Living Wage Employer and committed to equal opportunities and actively promote a diverse and inclusive working environment, and fairness for everyone.

Alongside our commitment to your professional and personal development, we also offer a generous benefits package including:
- Competitive salary
- 25 days annual leave plus Bank Holidays
- Company pension
- Enhanced Maternity and Paternity leave
- Small, friendly, and sociable teams with staff events
- Company profit bonus schemes
- Cycle 2work schemes
- Career opportunities for development and progression

title: Medical Administrator
description: We are looking for a reliable, enthusiastic and motivated individual who is committed to providing excellent patient care and is able to meet the requirements of a busy and growing Practice. We are a friendly family Practice, committed to delivering safe, high-quality services in innovative ways. As a large, well-established and forward-thinking GP Practice, we are proud to serve a registered patient population of approximately 42,000 patients. As our Practice continues to grow and develop, we are looking for someone to join our Medical Administrative Team who is flexible and adaptable to the needs of the service. This is a varied and rewarding front-line role, combining medical administration and reception responsibilities. You will play an important part in supporting our patients, clinicians and wider multidisciplinary team, helping to ensure the smooth and effective day-to-day running of the Practice. If you enjoy working in a busy environment, take pride in providing excellent customer service and are looking for a role where you can make a real difference to patients, we would love to hear from you. We welcome informal chats or visits, if you are interested, please contact Gillian Cawkill Head of HR & Governance gilliancawkill@nhs.net Unfortunately, we are unable to accept applications from individuals who require UK visa sponsorship. Applicants must have the right to work in the UK at the time of application. As a Medical Administrator, you will be one of the first points of contact for our patients and will provide a professional, helpful and compassionate service across a range of administrative and reception functions. Your duties will include, but are not limited to: Providing a friendly, professional and helpful first point of contact for patients, both face-to-face and by telephone. Handling telephone calls, digital contacts, practice emails and patient enquiries appropriately and efficiently. Undertaking medical administration and supporting the administrative elements of clinical triage. Maintaining patient confidentiality at all times. Contributing to the smooth and efficient running of the Practice. The role can be busy and fast-paced, and you will need to remain calm, professional and helpful when working under pressure. You will be expected to treat patients, visitors and colleagues with courtesy and respect and contribute to a welcoming and positive Practice environment. Working Hours 37.5 hours per week (full-time) preferred. We may also consider applications from candidates seeking a minimum of 30 hours per week. Working hours will be scheduled within the Practice's opening hours: Monday to Friday: 08:00-18:30 Saturday: 09:00-17:00 The role may include a regular requirement to work until 6.30 pm on Fridays. Candidates must therefore be able to work the required Friday late finish as part of their working pattern. We are looking for someone who is: Reliable, organised, and able to work effectively in a busy environment. Confident communicating with patients, colleagues and external organisations. Flexible and adaptable to the changing needs of a busy GP Practice. Able to manage competing priorities while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail. Professional, approachable and committed to delivering excellent patient service. Comfortable working across both administrative and reception functions. Able to work effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team. Confident using computer systems and willing to learn new systems and processes. Able to use their own initiative while also recognising when to seek advice or support. Committed to maintaining confidentiality and high standards of information governance. Able to demonstrate our values of Compassion, Respect, Learning, Quality and Integrity in their everyday work. Previous administrative experience and a strong background in customer service are essential. Previous experience of working within primary care, the NHS or another healthcare environment would be advantageous. However, we will provide training on Practice-specific systems and processes.
